what: [tooling] scripts/ci/check_matrix_config_agreement.py's arming test DISAGREES WITH THE RUNTIME on trail_decay, and qqq_trend_long_1d is sitting in the gap. The guard asks `_arms()` — any of (trail_decay_arm_r, trail_decay_stall_bars, trail_decay_tight_mult) is not None, a PRESENCE test imported from m20_fleet_exit_sweep.LEVER_DECLARED_KEYS. The RUNTIME asks `tight is not None and tight > 0 and (arm_r > 0 or stall > 0)` (src/runtime/trail_decay.py:149) — presence of tight_mult AND an actual arming condition. MEASURED 2026-09-25 by evaluating BOTH predicates against config/strategies.yaml (population: the three legs E41/E48 touched): qqq_trend_long_1d tight=2.0 arm=0.0 stall=0 → guard_arms=True, runtime_declared=FALSE; gld_pullback_1d tight=2.0 arm=0.0 stall=10 → both True (correct); scha_trend_long_1d after the E48 strip tight=None → both False (correct). qqq is the one divergent leg. Its matrix trail_decay cell reads `shipped` — legend: 'validated + live' — for a lever that cannot engage, and matrix-config-agreement passes over it because the orphan `trail_decay_tight_mult: 2.0` satisfies a presence test. HOW IT GOT THERE, and it is nobody's error: PR #12737 (E41) stripped qqq's trail_decay_arm_r and DELIBERATELY left trail_decay_tight_mult, saying so on the line ('removing it was not what was decided'). That was correct then; the orphan key is what makes the two predicates disagree. WHY THE E48 LANE DID NOT FIX IT: touching qqq_trend_long_1d's config is Tier-3 and outside the E48 dispatch (scha only), and changing the guard's predicate is a different concern from a Tier-3 config strip. Filed rather than carried past. THE FIX IS A CHOICE, NOT AN OBVIOUS PATCH — which is why this is queued and not done. (a) Make the guard ask the runtime's own predicate instead of a presence test. Most honest, but LEVER_DECLARED_KEYS is SHARED with the sweep's lever-off denominator, where PRESENCE is the right question ('was there anything to remove') — so the two uses must be separated rather than one silently changed under the other. (b) Propose stripping qqq's orphan tight_mult to the operator as a Tier-3 follow-on to E41, which makes config match runtime and the presence test correct again. (b) is cheaper; (a) is what stops the class recurring on the next leg stripped this way. CLASS: the same shape as RC-STORED-FIELD-READ-AS-ITS-NAME — a label ('declared') read as the measurement, while the predicate that actually decides sits one module away.
